chapter: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
title: Amalgamated radio broadcasts and the Palmer Brothers group
summary: He recalls the band's "Trouble in Paradise" radio number and an earlier group with the Palmer Brothers and John Kirby broadcasting on the Amalgamated network.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yeah, possibly. Our big number was 'Trouble In Paradise' over the Amalgamated Radio! As a matter of fact, that's the second time... I don't know if it was before... Was it before...? I was playing with the Palmer Brothers. When John Kirby left Fletcher's band, he organized a group with the Palmer Brothers and myself -- I was the piano player. We tried going around different places. And we broadcasted over the Amalgamated... See, WEAF, they had a feud or something with NB...I don't know if it was National Biscuit Company or National Broadcasting Company...! But they had some kind of a feud, and in between they brought this Amalgamated Broadcasting thing in, and I don't know long it lasted, but I remember it... It was
on Madison Avenue, I think it was 49th Street or 51st Street, 52nd Street, somewhere around there. I know we used to meet...
